text:
Kohl Rabi.
DIFFICULTY
Easy
1/5
HARVEST SEASONS
Summer / Autumn

Kohl rabi looks like a root crop, but the edible globe is really a swelling of the stem just above ground level. It is a cabbage relative with a sweet, mild brassica flavour and a delicate texture when grown quickly and picked young. The crop matures fast, often in about 8-12 weeks, making it useful as a half-season brassica. Quality depends on steady moisture and timely harvesting: drought, checks to growth or leaving the globes too long can make them hard and woody. Small young globes are good raw or cooked, while larger late varieties can stand into autumn if they keep growing steadily.

Quick facts
Sow

Apr–Jul in batches. Protect early Mar sowings. Aug for a late crop where the season allows.

Harvest

Jun – Nov

Germination

10 days

Sowing depth

5/8 in.

Row spacing

12 in. between rows

Yield (10 ft row)

20 globes

Plant spacing

Between plants: 6 in.; allow more room for giant varieties as directed on the packet

Ready in

About 8–12 weeks from sowing

Recommended varieties
Kolibri F1

A quick-growing purple kohlrabi with crisp white flesh. Pick the swollen stems young for tender raw or cooked slices.

Kossak F1

A pale-green kohlrabi with mild white flesh. A useful modern alternative to the traditional Vienna selections.

White Superschmelz

A large-growing pale kohlrabi. Useful for gardeners wanting a substantial crop rather than very small, quick-picked stems.

Key risks
Woody kohl rabi

Drought, growth checks, crowding or delayed harvesting make the swollen stem hard and fibrous.

Flea beetle

Tiny jumping beetles chew small round holes in young leaves, especially in warm dry weather.

Cabbage caterpillars

Caterpillars of cabbage white butterfly, cabbage moth and related pests chew holes in leaves.

Club root (finger and toe)

Swollen, distorted roots cause poor growth and wilting in sunshine.

VEGETABLE GUIDES
60
ROOT CROPS

Keep moisture steady.

Dry soil and growth checks make the stem woody.

Harvest while tender.

Do not wait for ordinary varieties to become oversized.

Hoe shallowly.

Avoid disturbing the roots while plants are small.

Soil & preparation
Choose a sunny site with fertile, well-drained soil. Test soil before adding lime.
Steady moisture matters: dry soil and growth checks make the swollen stem hard and woody.
Prepare the bed early with mature compost where needed. Give roots room and steady moisture; the edible globe is a swollen stem above ground.
Sowing & planting
Sow shallowly
Thin young plants
Sow 

Scatter seed thinly in shallow drills and cover lightly. Small batches give a succession of tender globes.

Plant out 

If starting in modules, harden off and plant before seedlings exceed 2 in. tall. Allow extra space for giant varieties.

Looking after the crop
Thin gradually from the first true leaves. Protect young plants from birds. Use collars or mesh where cabbage root fly is a problem.
Weed carefully. Check moisture and pests if growth slows; use an organic feed where fertility is poor.
Water in dry spells to prevent tough, woody globes. Give larger autumn crops extra room as growth slows in falling temperatures.
Harvesting & storage
Pull globes young and tender, from golf-ball to roughly tennis-ball size. Only grow suitable varieties larger; others become woody.
Late crops can stand through autumn and, in mild areas, into December. Protect with fleece or cloches before wintry weather and harvest while still tender.
Fresh-pulled globes are best. Keep briefly in cool conditions; quality declines after lifting.
Pests & diseases
Problem	What to look for	What to do
Woody kohl rabi	Hard, fibrous globes.	Water steadily; space well and harvest young.
Flea beetle	Tiny holes; jumping beetles.	Mesh young plants; keep growth steady.
Cabbage caterpillars	Holes; feeding caterpillars.	Hand-pick eggs and larvae; use fine mesh.
Club root (finger and toe)	Swollen roots; wilting.	Avoid infected soil; clean tools. Test before liming; no cure.
Cabbage root fly	Wilting; tunnelled roots.	Use collars or mesh on a rotated bed.
Slugs and snails	Holes; seedlings eaten.	Hand-pick at dusk; clear yellow leaves near seedlings.
Pigeons	Pecked or stripped leaves.	Net securely, clear of leaves.
Mealy aphid	Grey colonies; curled leaves.	Squash damaging colonies; encourage predators.
Final tips

Sow two or three small batches from April to June.

Try White Superschmelz for a July sowing and late crop.

Moist soil and timely picking keep globes tender.

VEGETABLE GUIDES
See also: Vegetable Troubles 106–111
